label: Foundational beings possibly absent is an alternative to foundational beings necessary at w
note: Lane F (#2103). Same CausalityFrame, world w and FoundationalAt parameters. Target: the necessity verdict 666f06a4 (every foundational being at w exists at every accessible world). Mechanism: two verified routes conclude the rival verdict, that every foundational being at w is ContingentAt, i.e. exists at w and is absent at some accessible world. One route is existence-conditional essentialism (f9d43a47, result 872a3832): a foundational being's own essential truths hold at a representable point lacking it, and no other being's essential truth requires it. The other is Kant's thesis with concept adequacy (b08d83a2, result 63ac77e7). Justification: both are recorded positive accounts of modality through essence, with their premises open in the corpus, not a bare negation. Incompatibility: NecessaryAt requires existence at every accessible world and ContingentAt an accessible world lacking the being, so both verdicts together exclude any foundational being at w (c5da5e62, open). Without a foundational being both hold vacuously. Neither verdict is established; no refutation of the rival is recorded.
